_meta.purpose: Healthy-adult normative ml histogram windows for TotalSegmentator PRIMARY_SEGMENT_GROUPS latch names (controller/ai/tseg/config.py). Keys must match those group names exactly; there is no catch-all default.

sections.soft_organs: Major soft-tissue latch groups from the TS total task
sections.skeletal: Primary skeletal latch groups (skull, spine, clavicles, ribs)

_meta.notes: Windows are literature-backed adult ranges for the closest matching tissue definition, then padded for sex, age, and partial FOV. Lobe windows use landmark whole-lobe GM+WM MRI volumes (not FreeSurfer cortical-GM-only). Subcortical windows use large FreeSurfer cohorts. Analytics omits truncal/column organs on head-limited series (no Chest/Abdomen latch mass) so whole-body spine/cord/organ norms are not applied to partial FOV. Extreme samples plot in underflow/overflow sentinel bins without stretching the main axis. Brainstem is retained in this JSON for PRIMARY_SEGMENT_GROUPS key coverage but is excluded from volume histograms (NORM_MISMATCH_EXCLUDED_ORGANS): Dataset409 CT labels systematically ~2× FreeSurfer MRI whole-brainstem; FreeSurfer 18–45 ml must not be re-enabled as a clinical norm until a method-matched TS-CT healthy band exists.
sources: Allen JS, Damasio H, Grabowski TJ. Am J Phys Anthropol 2002;118:341-358 (doi:10.1002/ajpa.10092): landmark MRI whole-lobe GM+WM volumes in 46 healthy adults (22–49 y). Bilateral observed ranges (min–max across sex): frontal ~319–551 ml, parietal ~182–333 ml, temporal ~180–311 ml, occipital ~64–123 ml; cerebellum ~113–185 ml; whole insula GM+WM ~14–26 ml (means ≈18.8 men / 16.4 women). Histogram windows pad those spans for age/FOV/CT vs MRI method differences. Note: Allen whole-insula GM+WM is not used for the TS ``insular_cortex`` latch (cortex/GM-class; see Faillenot).

Allen JS, Bruss J, Brown CK, Damasio H. Neurobiol Aging 2005;26:1245-1260 (doi:10.1016/j.neurobiolaging.2005.05.023): n=87 adults (22–88 y), same whole-lobe GM+WM definition; documents age-related decline used when padding lobe maxima/minima.

Faillenot I, et al. NeuroImage 2017;150:88-98 (doi:10.1016/j.neuroimage.2017.01.073): manual bilateral insular grey-matter volume 7.7±0.9 ml in 30 healthy adults (native space). Matches the TS Dataset409 ``insular_cortex`` tissue class better than Allen whole-insula GM+WM. Histogram window 5–15 ml ≈ mean±~3 SD with CT/method pad.
Cohen JD, et al. Cereb Cortex 2010 (PMC2813413): manual bilateral insular cortex ≈10.8 ml in typically developing controls — corroborates GM-cortex scale (~8–12 ml), not Allen ~16–19 ml means.

Potvin O, et al. NeuroImage 2016;137:9-20 (doi:10.1016/j.neuroimage.2016.05.016): FreeSurfer 5.3 subcortical norms, n=2,790 healthy adults (18–94 y). Brainstem regression intercept ≈21.4 ml (age/sex/eTIV/scanner covariates); healthy adult FreeSurfer brainstem is typically ~18–30 ml. Deep-nuclei windows follow the same cohort scales.

Sander L, et al. Front Neurosci 2020;14:609422 (doi:10.3389/fnins.2020.609422): FreeSurfer brainstem volumetry in healthy adults — unadjusted total brainstem means ≈28.3 ml (men) / 24.8 ml (women). Independent confirmation that MRI FreeSurfer whole-brainstem norms sit near ~25–30 ml, not ~50+ ml.

Igase K, et al. Sci Rep 2022;12:2055 (doi:10.1038/s41598-022-27202-x): FreeSurfer 6.0 brainstem subfield pipeline (whole brainstem + medulla/pons/midbrain) in n=182 healthy adults; used as an additional FreeSurfer-family reference. Manual midbrain+pons+medulla protocols (without peduncles/adjacent WM) can report ~6–8 ml — a different tissue definition, not a FreeSurfer whole-brainstem range.

Potvin O, et al. NOMIS (doi:10.1101/2021.01.25.428063): n=6,909 healthy adults (18–100 y) FreeSurfer 6 morphometry including brainstem subregions — cited for population scale; cortical-GM lobe sums are intentionally not used as TS lobe windows (different tissue class from landmark whole-lobe GM+WM).

TS Dataset409 brainstem (brain_structures task) on head CT often measures ~50–60 ml — roughly 2× FreeSurfer MRI whole-brainstem. Inflation is a label-definition / modality mismatch (CT soft-tissue boundaries; Dataset409 may include peduncles/adjacent tissue FreeSurfer excludes), not missing truncal FOV. Volume charts omit brainstem for this reason (see notes); do not silently widen 18–45 ml while still citing FreeSurfer.

TotalSegmentator total task exports vertebrae_C1–C7 (mapped to Head) plus spinal_cord; the analytics spine group still unions C+T+L+S. Head-limited scans typically only see C1–C2 — excluded from volume charts until cervical-only windows exist.
Cressoni M, et al. Crit Care 2014;18:R104 (doi:10.1186/cc13875): supine CT total lung volume mean ~4995 ml (men ~5757, women ~4136); large ICU CT series underpinning lungs window.
Kawel-Boehm N, et al. J Cardiovasc Magn Reson 2020;22:87 (doi:10.1186/s12968-020-00683-3): SCMR adult CMR chamber reference ranges; whole-heart TS mask ≈ chambers + myocardium (~250–650 ml healthy).
DeSouza SV, et al. Expert Rev Gastroenterol Hepatol 2018 (doi:10.1080/17474124.2018.1496015): pancreas volume meta-analysis (~71–83 ml typical; CT often ~40–120 ml).

Peters M, et al. / Courchesne E, et al. (as reviewed in Allen 2002): adult intracranial/whole-brain MRI means ~1100–1300 ml by sex; brain window 900–1600 ml pads healthy adult encephalic volume including measurement method spread.
Bigler & Woodard skeletal mass fractions + ICRP reference bone density (~1.9 g/cm³): approximate mineralized volumes for cranium, spine, ribs, clavicles (padded for TS mask FOV).
TS stomach is anatomical organ (wall ± lumen): empty-to-moderate fill typically tens–hundreds of ml; satiety MRI volumes can exceed 600 ml — axis padded accordingly.
